Nomifensine, a selective agonist at the Alpha adrenergic receptor, is known to activate this receptor, which in turn may influence the Gastrin/cholecystokinin type B receptor through downstream signaling cascades. This suggests that dextroamphetamine could exert its effects on the Gastrin/cholecystokinin type B receptor via a mechanism involving adrenergic receptor activation. The strength of the evidence is supported by the high confidence score, but further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction and the specific molecular pathway involved.
